Hit Vibes cover art

Saint Pepsi’s 2013 cover imitates an early-1980s record sleeve: a red square, floating parallelograms, a yellow wedge, and a thin swoosh on grainy grey.

Source
MusicBrainz: Hit Vibes (2013 digital release)
Creator
Saint Pepsi (Ryan DeRobertis)
Made
May 31, 2013 (digital release, KEATS//COLLECTIVE, per MusicBrainz)
Style
Vaporwave (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Retro, sunny, ironic
Evidence
Inspected the 900 × 900 front cover in the Cover Art Archive, in a scratchpad copy. Not stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Wikipedia names Skylar Spence (formerly Saint Pepsi) among the most popular future funk artists, and lists Saint Pepsi among the performers at the first vaporwave festival in 2019. Wikipedia: Vaporwave.

Observed

  • A large red square with a thin black outline sits on a grey, grainy ground.
  • A row of small red parallelograms with grey drop shadows crosses the top diagonally; a thin yellow wedge cuts down through the square.
  • A thin navy swoosh curves across the middle; HIT VIBES is printed faintly inside the square in large outline letters, and SAINT PEPSI in white thin italic capitals at the top left.

Why it belongs

Useful as a boundary case: it quotes the same 1980s source material as vaporwave through graphic pastiche, without the collage and digital artefacts.
